search_path: /Grid-converged force deficit in partially submerged free-rigid MPM coupling
exported_by: inspect_deep_searches + get_paper_info, Undermind MCP, workspace read live 2026-08-25
goal: Diagnose a systematic vertical force deficit of roughly 25 to 30 percent at PARTIAL submersion (20-30 percent of body volume under water, still water, no floor contact) in an MPM free-rigid coupling that sets the body centre-of-mass velocity to the mass-weighted average of the grid velocities beneath it, carries zero internal stress, and back-computes force from momentum change. Fully submerged the same scheme is within about 7 percent. The deficit does NOT shrink from grid 64 to 96 (margin moves 0.10 to 1.51 points), so it is grid-converged rather than a discretization artifact, and the equivalent pressure deficit is inconsistent across conditions (about 2700-5400 Pa versus about 6200 Pa in a directly measured profile), so it is not a constant pressure offset either. Four candidate mechanisms assessed: free-surface pressure boundary treatment in weakly-compressible MPM; stress-recovery and force-integration error at partial cell occupancy and cell crossing; velocity-projection coupling under-recovering force versus traction integration; artificial sound speed interacting differently at partial versus full submersion.
summary: A discrete interface/transfer bias, NOT a universal hydrostatic pressure offset, is the best-supported explanation. MPM force and stress accuracy is known to depend on particle quadrature, stress recovery, grid crossing and particle-to-grid projection [Ste00, Aco19b, Wal07], but NO cited paper directly documents a grid-converged underforce from assigning a free rigid body the grid-mass-averaged velocity. Force and stiffness integration and stress recovery degrade near discontinuities and cell boundaries [Aco19b]; quadrature error and non-smooth grid functions can prevent clean convergence [Ste00, Bau23]; projection accuracy depends on particle location and density [Wal07]. WCMPM is explicitly reported less accurate for free-surface flow, which is why incompressible variants introduce level-set pressure boundaries [Zha17c]. Velocity-based rigid coupling is documented but the located work does not show systematic force loss at a free surface [Miy23]. Strongest unresolved hypothesis: momentum imposed by velocity averaging is not equivalent to integrating interfacial traction, with the mismatch amplified where the body overlaps fluid/free-surface transition cells [Hu18, Fan20]. TOP-RANKED: Ste00 r=0.980, Zha17c r=0.960, Bau23 r=0.930, Che18c r=0.910, Wil20b r=0.880, Li22b (IFEMP, 10.1016/j.cma.2022.114809) r=0.870, Aco19b r=0.840.
